# TabPFN oversampling & resampling ensemble notebook

## Motivation

TabPFN is an in-context learner: training rows become the "prompt." Its internal feature-permutation / matrix mapping is stochastic (`random_state`), so **a single fit can vary across runs** even on identical data. This notebook tests whether **ensembling over resampled training contexts** stabilizes and improves holdout performance.

This is intentionally separate from [`tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb), which compares **feature-space synthesis** (SMOTE family) on processed arrays. Here we stay on **raw TabPFN-native features** and focus on **row-level resampling ensembles**.
    30|
## Evaluation protocol

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Data | Raw [`VLST.csv`](data/raw/VLST.csv) via `load_raw()` from [`tabpfn.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn.ipynb) |
| Split | **90/10 stratified** (`TEST_SIZE=0.10`, `random_state=42`) — user preference; ~518 train / ~52 test rows, ~7 test positives |
| Leakage | Drop `"Time since stent implantation"`; drop ID cols |
| Primary metric | **PR-AUC** on fixed test set (plus ROC-AUC, F1, F2, precision, recall) |
| Threshold | Per-method **10-fold stratified OOF** on train (`THRESHOLD_STRATEGY="f2"`, `beta=1.5`) — same policy as [`tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb) |
    40|| TabPFN config | `balance_probabilities=True`, `n_estimators=-1` (local) / cloud client fallback on Kaggle — mirror [`tabpfn.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn.ipynb) §3 |

**Note on small test set:** With ~7 positives in 10% holdout, point estimates will be noisy. The notebook will report **bootstrap CIs on test metrics** (reuse `bootstrap_ci` pattern from `tabpfn.ipynb` §6c) and optionally a **variance diagnostic** (baseline repeated across 10 seeds) to quantify TabPFN shuffle instability.

## Methods to implement

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph methods [Four methods]
    B[baseline]
    50|    Boot[bootstrap_ensemble]
    MC[mc_kfold_ensemble]
    RO[balanced_minority_oversample]
  end
  Train[X_train] --> B
  Train --> Boot
  Train --> MC
  Train --> RO
  B --> Avg[mean predict_proba]
  Boot --> Avg
    60|  MC --> Avg
  RO --> Avg
  Avg --> Test[X_test metrics]
```

### 1. Baseline TabPFN (`baseline`)
- Single model on full `X_train`, `random_state=42`.
- OOF threshold tuning via standard 10-fold CV.
- Reference for all comparisons.

    70|### 2. Bootstrap bagging ensemble (`bootstrap_ensemble`)
- **Aspect:** stochastic **with-replacement** resampling; prevalence roughly preserved; duplicate rows inflate minority presence organically.
- `B` stratified bootstrap samples of `X_train` (resample positives/negatives separately, same as `bootstrap_ci` in `tabpfn.ipynb`).
- Fit `B` TabPFN models; **mean** `predict_proba` on `X_test`.
- OOF: within each of 10 CV folds, draw `B` bootstraps from fold-train, average val predictions (method-consistent threshold tuning).

### 3. Monte Carlo K-fold ensemble (`mc_kfold_ensemble`)
- **Aspect:** **without-replacement** complementary subsets; each model sees ~90% of train (for K=10).
- `R` random seeds × `K` folds: for each seed, `StratifiedKFold(K, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)`.
- Per fold: fit on train indices, accumulate `predict_proba(X_test) / (R*K)`.
    80|- Reuse the averaging pattern from [`results.ipynb`](code/modeling/results.ipynb) `oof_train_test()` (`test_mean += pos_proba(m, X_test) / n_splits`).
- OOF: standard fold-held-out predictions, averaged across seeds where the same row appears in different fold positions across seeds (use per-row mean of all OOF estimates for that row).

**Default hyperparams (config cell):**

| Mode | `B` | `R` seeds | `K` folds |
|------|-----|-----------|-----------|
| `smoke` | 3 | 2 | 3 |
| `full` | 20 | 5 | 5 |

    90|### 4. Fourth technique: stratified minority oversampling (`balanced_minority_oversample`)
- **Why this one:** orthogonal to bootstrap (random row duplication) and MC K-fold (subset partitioning). It **targets class imbalance** by duplicating real minority rows until balanced — a classic oversampling axis not covered by the other two ensembles.
- Uses `imblearn.over_sampling.RandomOverSampler(random_state=42)` on training data only (no synthetic interpolation; safe on raw integer-coded categoricals).
- Single TabPFN fit on balanced context (~2× train rows).
- OOF: apply `RandomOverSampler` inside each CV fold on fold-train only (same leakage-safe pattern as `tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb`).

**Not chosen as 4th (documented in notes):**
- **SMOTE / ADASYN** — already in `tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb` (feature-space synthesis on processed data).
- **Seed-only ensemble** (same rows, varying `random_state`) — valuable diagnostic for internal shuffle variance, included as a **§variance diagnostic** section rather than a 5th primary method, since it is not row oversampling.

   100|## Notebook structure

New file: [`code/modeling/tabpfn_oversampling.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn_oversampling.ipynb)

| Section | Content |
|---------|---------|
| 0 Intro | Motivation, methods table, distinction from `tabpfn_synthesis` |
| 1 Install | `tabpfn`, `tabpfn-client`, `imbalanced-learn` (conditional pip) |

| 3 Paths + data | Reuse `_find_repo_root()`, `_resolve_paths()`; `RESULT_DIR = data/result/modeling_tabpfn_oversampling/` |
   110|| 4 Helpers | `load_raw()`, `make_tabpfn()`, `pos_proba()`, `select_threshold()`, `stratified_bootstrap_indices()`, `run_baseline()`, `run_bootstrap()`, `run_mc_kfold()`, `run_balanced_oversample()` |
| 5 Execute comparison | Loop four methods, collect metrics + test probability vectors |
| 6 Variance diagnostic | Run baseline 10× with seeds 42..51; plot PR-AUC / prob std on test |
| 7 Results | Leaderboard table, PR curves overlay, bar chart, bootstrap CIs |
| 8 Notes | Runtime cost, small-n caveat, when each method helps |

## Code reuse (copy/adapt, do not duplicate logic long-term)

Essential snippets to lift from existing notebooks:

   120|- [`tabpfn.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn.ipynb): `load_raw()`, `make_tabpfn()`, `select_threshold()`, `pos_proba()`, `bootstrap_ci()`
- [`tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb`](code/modeling/tabpfn_synthesis.ipynb): `run_method()` evaluation loop structure, per-fold sampler application

Core bootstrap sampler (new, ~15 lines):

```python
def stratified_bootstrap_indices(y, rng):
  pos = np.where(y == 1)[0]
  neg = np.where(y == 0)[0]
   130|  return np.concatenate([
    rng.choice(pos, size=len(pos), replace=True),
    rng.choice(neg, size=len(neg), replace=True),
  ])
```

## Outputs

Save under [`data/result/modeling_tabpfn_oversampling/`](data/result/modeling_tabpfn_oversampling/):

   140|- `tabpfn_oversampling_comparison.csv` — one row per method (metrics + train row counts)
- `tabpfn_oversampling_pr_curves.png` — overlaid PR curves
- `tabpfn_oversampling_pr_auc_bar.png` — bar chart with error bars if multi-seed diagnostics exist
- `tabpfn_oversampling_bootstrap_ci.csv` — per-method test metric CIs
- `tabpfn_oversampling_variance_diagnostic.csv` — baseline seed sweep
- `tabpfn_oversampling_manifest.json` — protocol metadata (`test_size=0.10`, `B`, `R`, `K`, etc.)

## Runtime expectations

- **Smoke mode:** ~15–25 TabPFN fits — minutes on GPU.
   150|- **Full mode:** ~100+ fits (bootstrap OOF is the bottleneck: `10 folds × B bootstraps`) — plan for 1–3 hours on GPU; progress logging per fold/bootstrap.
- Kaggle: auto-detect cloud client when no local GPU (same as other TabPFN notebooks).

## Comparison interpretation (for notebook discussion cell)

| Method | What varies | Expected effect |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| Baseline | Nothing | Best single-context reference; high seed variance |
| Bootstrap | Row composition (with replacement) | Reduces variance; may help minority signal via duplicates |
| MC K-fold | Disjoint train subsets across seeds | Diversifies context; averages partial-data experts |
   160|| Balanced oversample | Class ratio (1:1 duplicates) | More positive examples in context; risk of overfitting on ~74 positives |

Paired **Wilcoxon** test is not applicable on a single fixed test set; variance is addressed via bootstrap CIs and the seed diagnostic instead.
